title: Chicago Mayor Demands Data Center Moratorium
summary: Bloomberg's Miranda Davis joins Emily Graffeo on "Real Yield." Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson is pushing for a temporary moratorium on data centers, and signed an executive order on Tuesday to create new rules for any future developments. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: ‘SaaSpocalypse’ Risk From AI Reaches Beyond Private Equity
summary:
Bloomberg's Paula Seligson said that specific subsets of the software industry are especially at risk from the 'SaaSpocalypse' — the selloff of companies based around 'software-as-a-service — as artificial intelligence replaces software functionality for things like data visualization. Seligson said that right now investors are trying to figure out the reality of the risk around the 'SaaSpocalypse' and which companies most vulnerable. 
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Diversified Said to Near Deal for Elliott-Backed Birch
summary: Diversified Energy Co. is in advanced talks to acquire Elliott Investment Management-backed oil and gas company Birch Resources for more than $1.7 billion in cash, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: US Inflation Softens Ahead of Fed Data, Jackson Hole
summary: Senior Research Economist Sree Kochugovindan from Aberdeen discussed the recent US inflation data, describing it as a subdued core inflation print that has somewhat eased pressure on the Federal Reserve. Despite inflation remaining elevated and outpacing wage growth, the inflation report was considered a bit of a nonevent. Kochugovindan emphasized that there is still more economic data to be released and the upcoming Jackson Hole symposium remains a critical event for gauging the Fed's next moves. He suggested that it is still too early to definitively extrapolate the Fed's September rate decision based solely on the latest inflation figures. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stay In The Belly Of The Curve: BlackRock's Chaudhuri
summary: Gargi Chaudhuri, chief investment and portfolio strategist, Americas at BlackRock, joins Emily Graffeo on "Real Yield." The US government sold 30-year bonds at the highest interest rate in a quarter of a century, reflecting a relentless selloff that’s stirred speculation the nation will tilt borrowing further toward short-dated maturities. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: NYC Pied-a-Terre Tax Can Proceed for Now, Appeals Court Says
summary: The rollout of New York’s pied-à-terre tax can proceed for now after an appeals court temporarily put a hold on a Staten Island judge’s order blocking the plan.

title: Zaman: Rise in Japanese Long Yields Could Support Yen
summary: Bloomberg has learned Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government is supportive of a near-term rate hike by the Bank of Japan, with the next move likely either in September or October. This is after the yen edged closer to the key 160-per-dollar level. Mahjabeen Zaman, ANZ’s Head of FX Research spoke to Bloomberg’s Abeer Abu Omar on the efforts to shore up the currency. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: AMD Raises $4.75 Billion From Bond Sale as AI Demand Surges
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. raised $4.75 billion in the chipmaker’s biggest-ever US dollar bond offering, adding to a wave of debt tied to the artificial intelligence boom.

title: Still Seeing Credit Stress Under Surface: Cudzil
summary: Jerry Cudzil generalist portfolio manager, fixed income at TCW, joins Emily Graffeo on "Real Yield." As a flood of debt sales by US tech companies ripples through the credit market, it seems to be triggering an inadvertent rise in risk metrics for some of the world’s safest firms. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US, China Gap on Critical Minerals 'Won't Change Overnight,' Say REalloys CEO
summary: Lipi Sternheim, REalloys CEO, said that his company is working closely with the US Army to get a critical mining operation underway on US military base and that the US government's interest in expanding critical minerals mining in the US has not slowed. Sternheim said that expanding US capacity to the level of its competitors like China remains years away.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Workday Shares Surge After Report Silver Lake Is in Talks to Buy Company
summary: Workday Inc. shares jumped after a Reuters report that private equity firm Silver Lake is in talks to purchase the software provider.

title: US Pays Highest Yield on 30-Year Debt in Quarter of a Century
summary: Patrick McHenry, former Republican congressman from North Carolina and former House Financial Services Committee chairman, said that Thursday's bond sale is a 'wake up sign' for the country on government debt and deficit, as the US government sold 30-year bonds at the highest rate since 2001.  McHenry said that it is time for the government to take action on overspending, but that change has to begin with the American people raising the issue.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Two Sigma’s Overdeck Offered Wife $633 Million, Lawyer Says
summary: Two Sigma Investments’ billionaire co-founder John Overdeck schemed to leave his wife Laura “with as little as possible,” her lawyer said as the couple’s divorce trial began, an amount she pegged at $633 million.

Bloomberg's Laura Nahmias joins Emily Graffeo on "Real Yield." The rollout of New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s new pied-à-terre tax was temporarily blocked by a state court judge on Staten Island.

 (Source: Bloomberg)
